pending_commit.commit_message: Add base class to create/destroy mock config files I'm going to add a new unittest.TestCase to address b:142147850. In order to do so, I will want to create mock JSON config files. The pre-existing InheritanceTestCase already handled this nicely. This change moves the mockfile creation/deletion into an inherited base class so that I can reuse it for a different TestCase. Add model-level config overrides Previously, FAFT configs were only determined by the platform (board or variant) being tested. However, per the linked bug, we need a way to override the configs for only certain models. This change adds that feature. TEST=1. Run config_unittest.py 2. Add a logging.info(self.faft_config) to firmware_test.py. Run firmware_FAFTSetup on two octopus boards: a bobba360 and a meep. Verify that the octopus/bobba360 has bobba360 as highest precedence. Verify that the octopus/meep does not have a model-override. biod: Do not emit error in log when checking EC command support When checking whether a specific EC command is supported, we use the EC command EC_CMD_GET_CMD_VERSIONS. If this command returns with EC_RES_INVALID_PARAM, it only means the command to check is not support, and doesn't mean anything failed. Logging an error in this case would be confusing, so avoid emitting error. This does not affect any functionality. BUG=none TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-nocturne biod TEST=verified that the misleading error message no longer appears Change-Id: I589124a9a1981268cf5bd23e79fbfc8b6394f862 Signed-off-by: Yicheng Li <yichengli@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1860915 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Tom Hughes <tomhughes@chromium.org>

build_packages: Rebuild only on new revisions rebuild-if-unbuilt is too aggressive in triggering source rebuilds of packages and is tripping the referenced bug when rebuilding a package in both DEPEND and BDEPEND. Changing this option to only build on revision bump avoids triggering the bug and overall makes our build less eager to recompile packages from source. BUG=chromium:1014105 TEST=None Change-Id: I278d42d232686fbac347d8a8ba6adf0450bda19a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1867116 Tested-by: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

pytests/stylus: Add new argument for compensating UI orientation On some platforms, it's possible that the default orientation of panel and system are different. This may make stylus test confused because the toolkit draws UI according to system default orientation, while the underlying stylus signals are coming from evtest, which is using panel's coordination system. This CL adds a new argument to allow developer set UI orientation compensation manually. BUG=b:142611225 TEST=Run stylus test on Krane Change-Id: I85275bbf01f63d3fc68de2dfdde537975d25ad1f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1866351 Tested-by: Fei Shao <fshao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Fei Shao <fshao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pi-Hsun Shih <pihsun@chromium.org>

u2fd: Include allowlisting data when G2F enabled by policy This policy will only ever be used in conjunction with a server that expects to receive the allowlisting data; we should therefore always include it. We do not include the allowlisting data when G2F mode is enabled from crosh, as there is anecdotal evidence that some non-enterprise users are using G2F mode, and would be broken if we included the allowlisting data. BUG=b:135412897 TEST=enable g2f with policy, check allowlisting data is included Change-Id: I08f6d50d397cd34da4b17ed3c55ac0f70a075545 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1869089 Tested-by: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org>
